sources.entry: The Art of SLOs Workshop Materials

summary.name: The Art of SLOs
summary.one_liner: A hands-on workshop from Google's Customer Reliability Engineering team that teaches how to measure service reliability using Service Level Indicators (SLIs) and Service Level Objectives (SLOs).
use_cases: Training engineers on defining SLIs and SLOs
Running an internal reliability measurement workshop
Resolving development vs operations tension with error budgets
Practicing choosing proxy measures for user expectations
Reusing Google's SLO workshop materials under CC-BY-4.0
summary.what_it_does: The workshop explains how Google measures service reliability using SLIs and SLOs, and how SLOs and error budgets can manage reliability in a data-driven, user-focused way. It covers the qualities of good SLIs and applies a four-step process for developing SLIs to a fictional mobile game's server-side infrastructure. The practical part asks participants to build SLIs for more complex user interactions, then compare their work against example answers. The materials are aimed mainly at development and operations engineers and their management, with product people and business leaders recommended as well.
notable: Developed by Google's Customer Reliability Engineering team
Includes a hands-on exercise with a fictional mobile game example
Workshop materials released under CC-BY-4.0 with Google credited
Points to a self-paced Measuring and Managing Reliability course on Coursera for deeper study
caveats: Content is relatively technical and aimed mainly at engineers and their management
Designed for running a workshop with a team; the page does not describe a self-paced format itself
